findings.text: the later-revision copy was run with an overlay (2b8eb66f) whose apply report carries neither kept_identifiers nor kept_altered (logs/copy-b-apply-report.json), so "the same tool" was not applied and the identifier protection and kept-path receipt were never exercised at eccbb4bfd.
the 29 protected-identifier occurrences are stated twice in one paragraph in two wordings, so the landing record repeats a numeric claim it already made.

the sentence attributes 21 surfaces to current-name-consumer-inventory.html, whose measured table has 9 rows; the other 12 come from the brief's cutover conditions and the kept list, so the record overstates what that document contains.
format_report prints "old-name hits: N (kept K, leftover L)" while N also counts protected identifiers, so the measured N=194748, K=194719, L=0 does not reconcile in the line an operator reads.

the empty-scan and kept-search-blind guards, and apply's exit 1 on altered kept paths (scripts/rename/__main__.py:79), are unreachable by the suite; no test makes them fire, so a regression that disables them leaves the gate green.

cutover accounting is checked only against cutover.json itself and floors the inventory at 16 while it holds 21 surfaces, so up to five surfaces could be dropped from both the inventory and the steps and the gate would still pass.
